page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n1.medium is an entry-tier virtual instance configured with 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core across two threads. Operating on the x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz with 33 MB of L3 cache. System memory totals 4.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides no integrated local storage and features zero hardware accelerators or GPUs, requiring attached remote block storage for persistent data operations.

Benchmark testing indicates that the ecs.n1.medium operates primarily within entry-level performance tiers. It delivers a Geekbench single-core score of 959.0 and a multi-core score of 1698.0, placing it in the lower percentiles for compute execution. Computational passes under stress-ng yield 1108.59 in single-core and 2194.17 in multi-core metrics, while PassMark testing records a CPU aggregate score of 2676.41 and a database operations mark of 570.41. Memory transfers achieve 16.3 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 14.46 GB/sec for writes, alongside 1.9 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The instance offers low-overhead compute capacity suited for budget-conscious deployments where sustained high-throughput execution is not required. While the 1:2 compute-to-memory configuration delivers foundational processing capability with dedicated threads, the older CPU microarchitecture and absence of local high-speed storage constrain heavy I/O and parallel compilation tasks. Consequently, the ecs.n1.medium is best deployed for lightweight utility tasks, development and test instances, low-traffic microservices, and secondary background processes.
